newsitem.title: UK: Man sees sugar prices remaining in tight range.
newsitem.headline: Man sees sugar prices remaining in tight range.

text.p: World sugar prices are likely to remain trapped in narrow ranges as the global surplus predicted by analysts is offset by various buying interests, international trade house E D & F Man said in its latest report on Friday.
"Sugar prices are set to remain in a tight trading range with the market attracting support alternately from the trade and speculative interests," the report said.
"With the bulk of the potential surplus likely to appear in the whites market, white premium values may come under further pressure," it said.

Man added that the prospect of a new refinery in the Middle East could cause the shift away from refined sugar demand to raw sugar to rise to more than one million tonnes, even with the Dubai refinery operating at well below full capacity.

While noting talk of other refinery projects in the Middle East in countries such as Oman and Yemen, Man said the region as a whole had been operating in a free market climate with little import protection.
"If all these refinery projects were successful, the balance of trade would be altered in favour of raw sugar demand, depressing white sugar premium prospects," it said.
